cards.explanation: The answer is the heavens and the earth. Jeremiah, the prophet who is praying here, says it right up front: “You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm.” (Jeremiah 32:17) Babylon's army is outside, and he starts with who God is. I think that's a man who knows where to look first. Friends, that's some steady knees.
The answer is False. Jeremiah doesn't give God a short list of hard jobs. He says, “Nothing is too difficult for You!” (Jeremiah 32:17) He says it with the enemy camped around the city, too.

The answer is that God's eyes are on people to reward each one by his ways. Jeremiah says God's eyes are on all the ways of the sons of men, “…to reward each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.” (Jeremiah 32:19) So He's looking at each person's own ways. Not a crowd, not an average. Each one.

The answer is the land He swore to their fathers. Jeremiah says, “You gave them this land that You had sworn to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.” (Jeremiah 32:22) God made the promise, and God gave the land. I like when a promise comes with a delivery.

The answer is False. Jeremiah says they possessed the land, “…but they did not obey Your voice or walk in Your law.” (Jeremiah 32:23) So they did not obey, and the promise was kept on God's side. It's a heavy line, so we'll let it sit, friends.

The answer is disaster. Jeremiah says they did not do all God commanded, “…and so You have brought upon them all this disaster.” (Jeremiah 32:23) He's looking right at it while he prays, since the siege is outside. Disaster is the word he uses, so that's the word we keep.

The answer is True. Jeremiah points at the siege and says, “What You have spoken has happened, as You now see!” (Jeremiah 32:24) The ramps are up and the Chaldeans, the Babylonians, are fighting against the city. God spoke, and here it is. Jeremiah isn't arguing with it, friends; he's telling God what he sees.

The answer is to call in witnesses. Jeremiah says God told him, “Buy for yourself the field with silver and call in witnesses…” (Jeremiah 32:25) Silver, plus people watching. Think of it as a signed receipt, with people there to say they saw it. Even with the city handed over, God's instructions on the field stayed the same.

The answer is that they will set it on fire and burn it. God says the Chaldeans, the Babylonians, will come in, set the city on fire and burn it (Jeremiah 32:29). It's a hard line, and I think it's one to read slowly. God says it plainly, so we hear it plainly.

The answer is that they burned incense to Baal. God says some of those houses belong to people who provoked Him to anger “…by burning incense to Baal on their rooftops…” (Jeremiah 32:29). Baal was a false god. The verse also says they poured out drink offerings to other gods.

The answer is that He will remove it from His presence. God says, “Therefore I will remove it from My presence” (Jeremiah 32:31). It's serious. He says the city has aroused His wrath and fury from the day it was built until now. I think this one lands heavy, and we don't need to dress it up.

The answer is False. God lists kings and officials, priests and prophets, the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem as all having done evil to provoke Him (Jeremiah 32:32). So it wasn't only the common people. The list is long on purpose, I think. It's a sober line, so we'll take it as it is, friends.

The answer is backs. God says, “They have turned their backs to Me and not their faces.” (Jeremiah 32:33) That's a picture anyone gets. Nobody has to explain what it means to be turned away from. He says He taught them again and again, and they would not listen.

The answer is in the house that bears His Name. God says, “They have placed their abominations in the house that bears My Name, and so have defiled it.” (Jeremiah 32:34) That's the very house with His Name on it. I think that's what makes this line sting.

The answer is True. God says it was “…something I never commanded them, nor had it ever entered My mind, that they should commit such an abomination and cause Judah to sin.” (Jeremiah 32:35) This is a heavy part, friends, about sons and daughters passing through the fire to Molech, a false god. I think this one hurts. God says it never came from Him.

The answer is that He will gather them from all the lands. God says, “I will surely gather My people from all the lands to which I have banished them…” (Jeremiah 32:37). After all that burning talk, listen to that turn. He says He will gather them, and He says it with surely. That's how we know the story isn't over.

The answer is True. God says it plainly: “They will be My people, and I will be their God.” (Jeremiah 32:38) Short and simple, and it's the heart of the whole promise. After everything He just said, this is where He lands, friends.

The answer is that they will always fear Him for their good. God says He will give them one heart and one way, “…so that they will always fear Me for their own good and for the good of their children after them.” (Jeremiah 32:39) It's good for them, and good for their children after them. Notice how far ahead He's looking.

The answer is turning away from Him. God says, “…I will put My fear in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from Me.” (Jeremiah 32:40) Earlier God said they had turned their backs to Him and not their faces (Jeremiah 32:33). Here He promises that they will never turn away from Him. He's doing the heart work Himself.

The answer is False. God says He will bring on them not part of the good but “…all the good I have promised them.” (Jeremiah 32:42) Just as the disaster was real, the good will be too. All of it, friends.

The answer is fields. God says, “And fields will be bought in this land about which you are saying, ‘It is a desolation, without man or beast…’” (Jeremiah 32:43). Jeremiah himself was told, “Buy for yourself the field with silver and call in witnesses…” (Jeremiah 32:25). That's the same kind of deal, and his purchase was a sign of what God says is coming.

The answer is that He will restore them from captivity. God says it will happen “…because I will restore them from captivity, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 32:44) The reason is Him. He's the one who restores. Fields bought and deeds signed all over the land come from that promise.
